intro: Excerpts copied from the live Gamez source (C:\APPS\Gamez). Each shows the real code behind a capability and explains what it does. Keys live server-side (config.json / maia.db) or in the browser's localStorage — never hardcoded in WC2026.html. The betting math has a fixed, documented shape and the scoring is an openly-explained heuristic, not a prediction.

snippets.title: Serve the whole app same-origin
snippets.feature: Runs from file:// or served by the proxy at /
snippets.explanation: The proxy serves the single-file front end at GET /. Because the page is delivered by the same server it then calls for data and AI, everything is same-origin and CORS never bites. This one route is also what lets the PyInstaller .exe be self-contained: the proxy and the HTML ship together and the app loads from the proxy, not from disk.

snippets.title: The /snapshot bundle the page polls
snippets.feature: One call returns fixtures, standings, teams, players, odds
snippets.code:
@app.get("/snapshot")
def snapshot():
    return JSONResponse({
        "as_of": CACHE.get("as_of"), "source": CACHE.get("source"),
        "next_refresh_s": _next_refresh_s(),
        "openrouter": bool(OR_KEY),
        "fixtures": CACHE.get("fixtures", []),
        "standings": CACHE.get("standings", []),
        "teams": CACHE.get("teams", {}),
        "players": sorted(CACHE.get("players", []), key=lambda x: x.get("pps", 0), reverse=True),
        "kalshi": CACHE.get("kalshi", []),
        "errors": CACHE.get("errors", []),
        "disclaimer": DISCLAIMER,
    })
snippets.explanation: The single endpoint the front end polls. It returns the entire current state from the in-memory cache in one payload — live fixtures, the 12-group standings, scored teams + players (sorted by PPS), Kalshi odds, the data source, a freshness timestamp, and the ever-present disclaimer — so the page can render everything from one fetch.

snippets.title: Boot: warm cache, first fetch, scheduler
snippets.code:
def boot():
    """Warm the cache, kick an initial fetch, and start the refresh scheduler.
    Shared by the console launcher and the GUI (pywebview) launcher."""
    _load_cache()
    # initial fetch in the background so the server binds the port immediately
    threading.Thread(target=refresh, kwargs={"force": True}, daemon=True).start()
    sched = BackgroundScheduler(daemon=True)
    sched.add_job(refresh, "interval", minutes=CFG.get("refresh_minutes", 15),
                  id="refresh", max_instances=1, coalesce=True)
    sched.start()
snippets.explanation: On startup the proxy warm-starts from data/cache.json (so the app shows last-good data instantly), kicks the first live fetch on a daemon thread so the port binds immediately, and registers an APScheduler interval job to re-fetch and re-score every refresh_minutes (15). Shared by both the console and the windowed GUI launcher.

snippets.title: refresh() — never-raising data pipeline
snippets.feature: Fetch everything, score it, cache it, survive failures
snippets.code:
def refresh(force=False):
    """Fetch everything, score it, update the cache. Never raises."""
    ...
    # 4) score. Rated inputs (EA FC 'overall') use score_all_rated; raw match-stat
    #    inputs (API-Football / SAMPLE) use the percentile stat engine.
    players, teams = ([], {})
    src_players = raw_players or CACHE.get("players_raw") or []
    rated = bool(src_players) and (("overall" in src_players[0]) or src_players[0].get("source") == "EA FC 26")
    try:
        scorer = scoring.score_all_rated if rated else scoring.score_all
        players, teams = scorer([dict(p) for p in src_players])
    except Exception as e:
        errors.append(f"scoring: {e}\n{traceback.format_exc()[:400]}")

    with _LOCK:
        if fixtures:  CACHE["fixtures"] = fixtures
        if standings: CACHE["standings"] = standings
        if kalshi:    CACHE["kalshi"] = kalshi
        if players:
            CACHE["players"] = players; CACHE["players_raw"] = src_players; CACHE["teams"] = teams
        CACHE["source"] = source; CACHE["errors"] = errors
        CACHE["as_of"] = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
        _save_cache()
snippets.explanation: The heart of the proxy. Each source (ESPN, players, Kalshi) is fetched in its own try/except and any error is collected rather than thrown, so one dead source never blanks the app. It then chooses the right scorer — score_all_rated for EA FC 'overall' ratings, the percentile score_all for raw match stats — and atomically updates the locked in-memory CACHE, keeping the previous good values for anything that failed this cycle.

snippets.title: ESPN fixtures → phase + real-team flags
snippets.feature: Live board + real bracket vs TBD placeholders
snippets.code:
data = _get(f"{ESPN_BASE}/scoreboard", params={"dates": "20260611-20260719", "limit": 400})
for ev in data.get("events", []):
    ...
    na, nb = nm(home), nm(away)
    ph = _classify(dt, ev.get("name", ""))
    grp = (groups.get(na) or groups.get(nb) or "") if ph == "Group" else ""
    out.append({
        "ph": ph, "grp": grp, "dt": dt, "date": dt[:10],
        "a": na, "b": nb,
        "aReal": _is_real_team(na, groups), "bReal": _is_real_team(nb, groups),
        "sa": sc(home) if status in ("in", "post") else None,
        "sb": sc(away) if status in ("in", "post") else None,
        "status": status,
    })
snippets.explanation: Pulls the real World Cup schedule from ESPN (no API key), normalises each match to the page's shape, buckets it into a phase via _classify() (the real 2026 schedule windows), tags the group letter, and crucially flags aReal/bReal — whether each side is a confirmed team or a 'Winner of…' placeholder — which is what lets the front end draw a real bracket that fills in as teams qualify.

snippets.title: EA FC 26 ratings → national squads
snippets.feature: Default squad-strength source (free, no key, no quota)
snippets.code:
for row in csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text)):
    ovr = _toint(row.get("overall")) or 0
    if ovr <= 0: continue
    nat = (row.get("nationality_name") or "").strip()
    if not nat: continue
    team = FIFA_TEAM_ALIAS.get(nat, nat)
    primary = (row.get("player_positions") or "").split(",")[0].strip().upper()
    by_team.setdefault(team, []).append({
        "name": (row.get("short_name") or row.get("long_name") or "").strip(),
        "team": team, "pps": float(ovr), "overall": ovr,
        "position": primary, "group": FIFA_POS.get(primary, "MID"),
        "national": bool((row.get("nation_team_id") or "").strip()),
        "minutes": 900, "pps_conf": 0.85, "source": "EA FC 26"})
snippets.explanation: The realistic squad-strength source NOW: the 2026 squads aren't published, so this maps real EA FC 26 player ratings to national teams. Each player's club-derived 'overall' becomes their PPS, FIFA_TEAM_ALIAS reconciles EA's spellings (Korea Republic → South Korea) to ESPN's, and players with a national_team_id are preferred. The ~11 MB CSV is cached weekly on disk so it downloads rarely.

snippets.title: Kalshi odds with self-healing discovery
snippets.code:
# Self-heal: if the known series gave nothing, discover live WC series and retry.
if not out and discover:
    extra = [s for s in discover_kalshi_series() if s not in series_list]
    if extra:
        out = fetch_kalshi(series=extra, max_pages=max_pages, discover=False)
out.sort(key=lambda x: x.get("prob", 0), reverse=True)
return out
snippets.explanation: Kalshi renames/derives its World Cup series ticker per tournament and hasn't listed the markets yet (they open near the event). Rather than hard-code a ticker that may not exist, fetch_kalshi() tries the known series first and, if they yield nothing, scans open Kalshi events by keyword to discover the live series and retries — so the odds feed self-heals the moment Kalshi lists the markets. All fetched server-side to dodge browser CORS.

snippets.title: Squad Strength from a projected XI
snippets.feature: Player scores → team score with star + depth
snippets.code:
# spine-weighted mean of XI
num = sum(p.get("pps", 0) * SPINE.get(p.get("group", "MID"), 1.0) for p in xi)
den = sum(SPINE.get(p.get("group", "MID"), 1.0) for p in xi)
base = num / den if den else 0.0

# star non-linearity
top = max((p.get("pps", 0) for p in xi), default=0)
star = 0.12 * max(0.0, top - 70.0)            # up to ~3.6 for a 100 PPS star

# bench depth (next best 5)
bench = leftovers[:5]
depth = (mean([p.get("pps", 0) for p in bench]) / 100.0 * 5.0) if bench else 0.0

sss = max(0.0, min(100.0, base + star + depth))
snippets.explanation: Turns a roster of player scores into a single 0-100 Squad Strength Score. It builds a projected best XI (1 GK / 4 DEF / 3 MID / 3 ATT), takes a spine-weighted mean (a strong GK/spine counts more), adds a star bonus so one elite player can swing a knockout tie, and a bench-depth term because 7 games in 4 weeks rewards rotation. Transparent and bounded — a heuristic, openly defined.

snippets.title: Position-aware percentile PPS
snippets.feature: Player score from per-90, percentile-normalised stats
snippets.code:
pps = raw * 100.0
# small-sample shrinkage toward neutral 50
mins = p.get("minutes") or 0
w_mins = min(1.0, mins / 450.0)          # ~5 full matches = full trust
pps_adj = 50.0 * (1 - w_mins) + pps * w_mins
# confidence: minutes coverage * metric richness
present_metrics = sum(1 for m in all_metrics if p.get(m) is not None)
richness = min(1.0, present_metrics / 8.0)
p["pps"] = round(max(0.0, min(100.0, pps_adj)), 1)
p["pps_conf"] = round(max(0.0, min(1.0, w_mins * 0.6 + richness * 0.4)), 2)
snippets.explanation: The stat-based path (used for API-Football / SAMPLE inputs, not pre-rated EA FC data). Counting stats are converted per-90 and percentile-ranked within the player's position group, weighted by category. Crucially it shrinks a low-minutes player's score toward a neutral 50 (small-sample protection) and attaches a confidence from minutes coverage and how many metrics were actually present — so thin data is visibly less trusted.

snippets.title: The locked betting math
snippets.explanation: The fixed, documented betting-window math. A single per-match win probability p is raised to the number of rounds a team must survive to win a bet placed at that phase (winProb = p^rounds), payout is the inverse plus a fee, and value blends payout potential with an information-quality weight INFO that grows from Group (0.15) to the Final (1.0). The result is a structural lens showing R16/QF as the sweet spot — explicitly not a prediction.

snippets.title: Marry squad strength with real form
snippets.explanation: Combines the proxy's squad strength (SSS) with the team's actual tournament form (TFS, derived from goal-difference per game in the entered/live standings). The weight w = gp/(gp+3) shifts toward real results as more games are played, then the combined 0-100 score maps to a per-match win probability p (clamped 0.05-0.97). It falls back to form-only when no squad model exists — and that p is exactly what feeds phaseMetrics().

snippets.title: Live board assembly from /snapshot
snippets.feature: Real ESPN schedule becomes the board; manual fills gaps
snippets.explanation: Decides what the board shows. When the proxy is connected (liveOn()), the real ESPN fixtures ARE the board; otherwise built-in SEED fixtures are used. A live source score always wins — manually-entered scores (persisted in localStorage as OVER, keyed by a match signature) only fill matches no source has yet — and the board is sorted by phase then kickoff.

snippets.title: OpenRouter proxy with server-side key + free fallback
snippets.feature: Shared AI works with no browser key
snippets.explanation: Relays a chat completion to OpenRouter using the SERVER-SIDE key (config.json or the shared key from maia.db) so the browser never sees it. Because the free tier is intermittently rate-limited, a :free model that returns 404/429/502/503 walks the FREE_FALLBACKS chain so the chat still answers — but a genuine error (auth/credits/bad request) stops the loop instead of being masked.

snippets.title: Tunnel-only AI access gate
snippets.feature: Gate the shared AI; instant lockout on code change
snippets.explanation: Lets the owner share the AI over the public tunnel without giving away unlimited free-tier usage. _via_tunnel() detects Cloudflare's injected headers, so only tunnel traffic is checked — the owner's own local/exe use is never gated. When an access password is set, a tunnel request must carry a matching X-AI-Access header or it gets the friendly AI_LOCKED_MSG. The password is re-read from config.json on every call, so changing it locks out stale users instantly.

snippets.title: One AI call path, many providers
snippets.explanation: A single front-end function branches by chosen provider: Ollama and keyless OpenRouter go through the proxy (no CORS, server-side key, optional access code), while Anthropic/Google/Azure/OpenAI-compatible providers are called directly with a key the user pasted into localStorage. The keyless-OpenRouter branch is what makes the shared AI work out of the box, and systemPrompt() embeds a JSON snapshot of the live panels so the analyst answers only from on-screen data.

snippets.title: Shared OpenRouter key from maia.db
snippets.feature: Reuse the ecosystem's one key, never hardcoded
snippets.explanation: Gamez doesn't manage its own AI key. config.json wins if set (used for portable builds given to a friend), but on the owner's machine it's left blank and the proxy reads the shared system.openrouter_api_key straight out of Maia's maia.db — the same pattern MapSnap uses — so the whole ecosystem shares one free-tier key with nothing duplicated.

snippets.title: Local-only config write with hot reload
snippets.feature: Edit settings without exposing secrets over the tunnel
snippets.explanation: The config holds secrets, so both reading and writing it are refused over the public tunnel (_via_tunnel guard) — only direct localhost/exe access can touch it. A successful write reloads CFG in place so most settings (refresh interval, player source, access password) take effect on the next refresh cycle without a restart; only the listen port still needs one.
